Durga idol made with 1.5 lakh matchsticks draws crowds in Satkhira
item.description:
A Durga idol crafted from more than 150,000 matchsticks and over 10kg of silk thread has become a major attraction ahead of this year’s Sharadiya Durga Puja in Satkhira.
The unusual idol, created at the Dhulihar-Brahmarajpur Sri Sri Durga Puja Mandap in Satkhira Sadar, is drawing visitors eager to admire its intricate craftsmanship.
With Mahalaya observed on Friday, marking the beginning of the festive season, temples and puja mandaps across the district are bustling with activity as artisans put the finishing touches to idols and decorations.
At the Brahmarajpur temple, more than 150,000 matchsticks have been meticulously attached to a clay idol to create elaborate patterns requiring exceptional precision and patience. Even a minor mistake could ruin the design, making the work particularly challenging.
Idol maker Nabodip Sarkar said he had seen similar artwork in Kolkata in 2023 and decided to introduce the technique in Satkhira.
Four artisans have been working around the clock, sometimes until 2am or 3am, to complete the idol, he said. Sarkar has also been commissioned to make Durga idols at four locations this year, including in Satkhira and Kushtia.
He said special adhesives and chemicals had been used to neutralise the combustible properties of the match heads, with precautions taken to minimise safety risks.
Amit Kumar Ghosh, assistant treasurer of the Brahmarajpur Sarbojanin Sri Sri Durga Mandir committee, said the artisans’ fees alone amounted to around Tk1.3 lakh, while the total budget for this year’s celebrations was approximately Tk5 lakh.
The puja, organised by zamindar Pashupati Mitra, has been celebrated for more than 200 years, he said.
Unconventional idols have become something of a tradition at the temple. Last year, an idol made with 100kg of Chinigura rice attracted visitors from far and wide. Encouraged by the response, the organisers decided to experiment with another unusual material this year.
Safety concerns surrounding the matchstick idol prompted an inspection and trial on September 16 involving Satkhira Sadar Upazila Nirbahi Officer Arnab Kumar Dutta, the officer-in-charge of Satkhira Sadar police station and officials from Fire Service and Civil Defence.
Closed-circuit television cameras have also been installed throughout the temple premises to ensure the safety of the idol and visitors.
Preparations are underway at puja mandaps across the district, including in Shyamnagar, Kaliganj, Debhata, Assasuni, Tala and Kalaroa. Alongside traditional clay idols built over bamboo and straw frameworks, artisans are experimenting with different decorative designs.
The festival also provides employment for potters, bamboo and wood craftsmen, painters and decoration workers.
Biswanath Ghosh, general secretary of the Satkhira district unit of the Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad, said 590 puja mandaps would host celebrations in the district this year, up from 587 last year.
Mahalaya on Friday marked the beginning of the countdown to the festival. Maha Shashthi will be observed on October 17, while the celebrations will conclude with Bijoya Dashami on October 21.
According to Hindu tradition, the goddess will arrive on horseback and depart by boat this year.

item.title: Gopalganj university school faces existential crisis
item.description:
Gopalganj Science and Technology University School and College is facing an uncertain future as its teachers and employees have gone without salaries and allowances for about seven years, while students struggle with inadequate classrooms, poor sanitation, unsafe drinking water, and the lack of a playground.
Established on the university campus in 2017, the school initially had 16 teachers and three employees and enrolled 675 students in its first year. The college section was never opened.
The teachers and employees have not been receiving salaries and allowances since 2019. The school received academic recognition from the Dhaka Education Board in 2020.
It was later relocated from beside the university library to an area near the vice-chancellor’s residence. Teachers, students, and guardians said its condition deteriorated after the relocation, causing enrolment to decline. The school now has only 160 students from pre-primary to Class 10.
Students said classrooms lack adequate fans and roofs leak during rain. They also complained about poor sanitation and a lack of safe drinking water.
“There are bushes near the washrooms where snakes are seen. Water also leaks through the classroom roof when it rains,” said Class 5 student Fariduzzaman Ahsaf.
Class 7 student Riyan said the school had no playground and students had to attend classes in extreme heat.
Guardians said teachers’ dedication was the main reason they continued sending their children to the school. Saila Zaman, mother of a Class 6 student, said the campus environment was good but facilities were inadequate. “Two classes are sometimes held in the same room. There are not enough fans, and there are many other problems,” she said.
Assistant teacher Aleya Begum said teachers had been running the school with money collected from students and contributions from their own pockets. “We have not received salaries or allowances for nearly seven years. It has become extremely difficult to support our families. Some teachers travel from Khulna, Kotalipara and other areas to attend school regularly,” she said.
Vice-Chancellor Prof Dr Md Sohel Hasan said the school had no formal approval and was not included in the university’s organogram. “There is a school here with teachers, employees and students. I will form a committee to include it in the organogram and then seek University Grants Commission approval for appointing teachers and employees,” he said.
The vice-chancellor further said he would take necessary steps to resolve the school’s problems and improve educational opportunities for the students.

item.title: Malaysian national jailed after remand in 4.5kg gold case
item.description:
A Malaysian national arrested with 4.5kg of gold worth nearly Tk8 crore at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka has been sent to jail after a six-day remand.
On Sunday, investigation officer SI Mahbub Hossain of Airport Police Station produced Yang Don Seow, 43, before the court and sought an order to send him to jail. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Kamal Uddin passed the order to send him jail following the petition.
SI Abu Bakar Siddique of the prosecution division confirmed the matter, adding that the accused had not sought bail.
The court had placed him on a six-day remand last Monday.
He was arrested around 4:00am on October 4 after customs officials recovered nine gold bars weighing a total of 4.5kg from him. The gold was valued at approximately Tk7.95 crore, according to the National Board of Revenue (NBR).
The NBR said Yang arrived in Dhaka from Kuala Lumpur on Malaysia Airlines flight MH0196. Customs officials monitored him after the flight landed and searched him as he passed through Green Channel-1 after collecting his baggage.
The recovered gold comprised four bars weighing 1kg each and five weighing 100g each. The 24-carat gold bars were concealed under his shirt in a black cloth belt.
Assistant Revenue Officer Moniruzzaman of the Dhaka Customs House's Customs Preventive unit filed a case against him under the Special Powers Act at Airport Police Station on Sunday.

‘Going bankrupt’: Iran shopkeepers struggle as war dims demand
item.description:
At a Tehran bazaar where fragrant herbs and spices whet the appetite, shopkeeper Nasir says locals once bought his nuts by the kilo but soaring prices caused by the US-Iran war have eaten into sales, leaving businesses fighting for survival.
The marketplace in the Iranian capital’s north would usually be abuzz with customers, but shops now sit mostly empty with only small numbers of people walking its old narrow paths, a jarring shift for the sellers shouting to promote their goods.
“There used to be customers who bought two to five kilograms. Now, they’re down to buying one kilogram or half a kilogram,” said the 61-year-old.
“Prices are truly high. We all know it, and it would be a lie to say otherwise.”
Nasir called on authorities to stabilise the currency so businesses could plan ahead.
“We’re left in limbo, everyone is,” said the fruit and nut seller.
“They need to stabilise the dollar exchange rate.”
Iran’s economy has been battered by years of sanctions, but the conflict that began in February with US-Israeli attacks and an American blockade of the country’s ports has put extra strain on daily life.
Rising inflation, nearly 90% year-on-year in September according to official figures, and erratic currency exchange fluctuations have driven up the cost of everyday items. Food prices have more than doubled since last year.
At the bazaar, a historic covered market in Tehran’s Tajrish square, locals surrounded by Iranian flags and Persian signage try to escape the economic gloom, scanning sweets, jewellery, traditional garments and cuts of meat before their weekend begins.
In an alley, a street artist plays a guitar while another drums his hands on a box to draw tips from passersby.
But across the commercial district, many struggles to see a future for their businesses.
“It is a desperate, last-ditch struggle. Manufacturers are going bankrupt, laying off staff and closing shops, and the impact inevitably reaches us,” said Ali Nowruzi, 36, who runs a sportswear shop in the bazaar.
The businessman now orders only a few items for display on his shop’s shelves to stop them from looking bare like his warehouse, which he says lies empty due to lack of demand.
“We have absolutely no plan for the future. When people don’t come to buy... it effectively spells bankruptcy for the business,” he said, citing rising rent and utility bills.
“We just need some stability.”
Many shoppers, whose purchasing power has weakened since the outbreak of war, are seen leaving the bazaar without buying anything.
Azadeh, a 45-year-old woman currently out of work, says she just goes there to “watch the shops”.
Mounting pressure over the war saw Iran’s GDP contract 10.1% year-on-year between late March and late June, according to official figures.
The rial traded at around 2.7 million to the dollar on the unofficial market in the past week, compared with about 1.7 million before the war.
The minimum monthly wage that stood at around $120 a year ago has fallen to $65.
The country’s economy minister has rejected predictions of an imminent economic collapse, accusing Iran’s foes of trying to fuel public anxiety and drive up exchange rates.
Azadeh offers a price comparison of a kitchen cloth bought several months ago for 22 cents. She says that item now costs $1.10, five times more.
“It shows that prices haven’t just gone up -- they’ve truly skyrocketed,” she said.
She has stopped buying some fruits and says she can no longer afford holidays.
“We aren’t meant to just exist, we’re meant to actually live, right?” she asked.
Car mechanic Mojtaba Rezaei says his customers have “dropped to a tenth of what it was” because “goods now cost two or three times as much”.
“I actually feel embarrassed telling prices to customers. People just come in, ask the price, and leave,” the 57-year-old told AFP at the bazaar.
“So many things -- buying clothes, going out for leisure, dining at restaurants -- have all been cut out of our lives.”

item.title: 109 migrants dead, 116 missing in boat wreck off Djibouti
item.description:
At least 109 migrants died, including 15 children, and some 116 went missing when a boat sank off the shores of Djibouti overnight on October 8-9, a UN agency said Sunday.
Survivors said the vessel -- which was carrying 305 people from Djibouti to Yemen -- capsized north of the Djibouti town of Obock, according to a statement from the International Organization for Migration (IOM).
“This is a devastating loss of life. Our thoughts are with the survivors and the families who have lost loved ones or remain without news of their relatives,” said Alexandre Coissac, IOM chief of mission in Djibouti, in the statement.
He said IOM teams were on the ground alongside Djiboutian authorities to provide emergency aid.
“This tragedy is a stark reminder of the dangers faced by migrants along this migration corridor as they seek economic opportunities” by trying to cross the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to Yemen and then to reach Gulf countries.
Among the 109 bodies recovered were 52 men, 42 women and 15 children -- nine girls and six boys -- the statement said.
More than 80 people survived the shipwreck, all Ethiopian nationals.
“Poverty, insecurity and the growing impacts of climate change drive many to undertake this journey, despite mounting instability across the Middle East,” the IOM said.
Yemen is stricken by fighting between the Saudi-backed government and Tehran-backed Houthi rebels, who have joined in the regional conflict involving the US and its allies against Iran.
IOM said it was assisting 64 survivors at a migrant centre in Obock.
“Djiboutian authorities are continuing search and rescue operations as fears grow for those still missing.”
Since September 10, the IOM detected more than 20,000 crossings to Djibouti from Ethiopia.
In 2025, more than 900 migrants died or went missing along the sea route to Yemen and the number attempting the journey increased by 18 percent, it said.
A shipwreck in March 2026 left nine people dead and 45 missing.
IOM spokesman Kennedy Omondi Okoth told AFP this week that most of the people attempting the journey were from Ethiopia or Somalia.
He said many of them were ending up stuck in Djibouti.
The IOM urged “donors and partners to strengthen support for Djibouti’s response, including search and rescue operations and life-saving assistance”.

item.title: Pennsylvania shooting kills 9, including suspect
item.description:
Nine people, including two young children and a pregnant woman, were killed in a shooting at a residence in Erie, Pennsylvania, on Friday, with the suspected gunman dying from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound, police said Saturday.
According to NBC News and USA TODAY, the victims included seven family members of the 45-year-old suspected shooter and a family friend. The victims ranged in age from 22 months to 51 years, according to police accounts.
Erie police received a gunshot detection alert at about 4:52pm Friday and responded to a residence on the 700 block of Perry Street. Police Chief Rick Lorah said officers arrived about three minutes after the alert and found two women, aged 51 and 37, fatally wounded outside the house.
Investigators reviewing a neighbour’s doorbell camera footage found that the women appeared distressed as they approached the residence and knocked on the door seeking assistance. Audio from the footage appeared to capture muffled gunfire from inside the house before the suspect came outside and shot the women as they ran towards him, Lorah said.
The suspect then returned inside the residence. Police reported no further gunshots after officers arrived.
Officers initially could not establish contact with anyone inside the house. According to a statement from the Erie city government cited by USA TODAY, police secured the area before a special weapons and tactics (SWAT) team entered and cleared the residence.
The officers initially saw no movement inside and heard no gunshots or cries for help. Police said they had limited information about whether the suspect remained inside or posed an ongoing threat. The city clarified that the deaths occurred before officers entered the house and that the incident did not involve a prolonged standoff or a delay caused by obtaining a search warrant.
After deploying a robot to assess the scene, officers entered the residence and found several victims. A 5-year-old boy and a 22-month-old girl were found on the first floor, while four other victims — women aged 24 and 44 and men aged 19 and 21 — were discovered in a stairwell on the second floor.
The suspected shooter, a 45-year-old man whose identity had not been publicly released, was found dead on the second floor. Police recovered a .40-caliber handgun registered to him, Lorah said.
One of the victims found inside the house was eight months pregnant. Police said the victims found inside lived at the residence, while the two women killed outside did not. One of the women was a family friend, while the other was related to a family member, according to police accounts.
Erie County Coroner Lyell Cook said his office was working to confirm the identities of the deceased. Authorities had not publicly released their names or announced final determinations on the causes of death as of Saturday afternoon, USA TODAY reported.
Lorah described the scene as the worst he had encountered during his law enforcement career. He said investigators were examining evidence, reviewing cellphones and interviewing relatives and witnesses to establish what led to the shooting.
Although the police chief said mental health could be a factor, he stressed that investigators had not established a motive. He also noted that police had previously had contact with the suspected shooter, with the last interaction he recalled occurring in 2022.
Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro said he had spoken with Erie Mayor Daria Devlin and offered the state government’s support to the victims’ families and the wider community.
“My heart breaks for this family,” Shapiro wrote on social media, adding that he and his wife were praying for the victims’ loved ones and the Erie community.
Devlin said the city was coordinating with crisis services, behavioural health providers, schools and community organisations to provide support to affected residents. Erie County District Attorney Elizabeth Hirz also urged the public to avoid spreading rumours and unverified information while the investigation continues.
The shooting occurred on the same weekend that two Philadelphia police officers were shot early Saturday. Shapiro described the incidents as a dark day for Pennsylvania.
Erie is located about 190 kilometres north of Pittsburgh.

item.title: Flash flood sweeps away 65 houses in Nepal, 5 missing
item.description:
Five people are missing after a flash flood swept away 65 houses and damaged four bridges along Nepal’s Budhi Gandaki River in the central part of the country on Sunday, according to reports by AP.
The flood struck Gorkha and Dhading districts after a landslide at Chumanubri Rural Municipality in Gorkha temporarily blocked the river, according to the Nepal Army. The river later breached the blockage, sending a sudden surge of water, mud, and debris through settlements along its banks.
Armed Police Force spokesperson Netra Bahadur Karki said all five missing people were reported from Gorkha district, adding that authorities were still collecting information about the extent of the damage.
The flood destroyed two motorable bridges and two suspension bridges, disrupting local connectivity.
The Nepal Army airlifted 36 people to safer locations following the disaster, while security forces continued search and rescue operations.
The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority evacuated residents from vulnerable areas and urged people living nearby to move to safer locations. Authorities also warned residents to remain vigilant as the situation developed.
Videos circulating on social media showed floodwaters rushing through steep mountain valleys, carrying away houses and other structures. The full extent of the damage and the number of affected settlements remained unclear.
The flooding also raised concerns in Arughat, a riverside town along a highway connecting Kathmandu with other parts of the country, where social media posts indicated that warnings had prompted evacuations.
The Budhi Gandaki River flows into the Trishuli River, an important waterway near Nepal’s capital, Kathmandu.
The disaster comes as Nepal continues to recover from devastating floods in August along its mountainous border with China, which reportedly left more than 1,400 people dead and thousands missing.
Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s office subsequently announced the end of search and rescue operations for additional victims of the earlier disaster, with authorities shifting their focus to recovery and reconstruction. Damaged roads and bridges, particularly in remote areas, have hampered the delivery of relief supplies.
The government estimates that reconstruction following the earlier floods will cost $4.77 billion. Nearly 33,000 people were affected, while about 7,500 houses were damaged or destroyed.

Dhaka ranks 6th most polluted city
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 6th among the world's most polluted cities on Sunday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 166 at 8:31am.
The air quality was classified as "unhealthy", meaning the concentration of pollutants in the air has reached a level that could pose health risks to the general population, according to the AQI scale.
Kolkata in India ranked first with an AQI score of 187, while Singapore ranked second with a score of 184, followed by Hanoi in Vietnam in the third place with an AQI score of 178.
According to AQI standards, a reading between 101 and 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while 151 to 200 is classified as "unhealthy". A reading between 201 and 300 is considered "very unhealthy", while levels above 301 are deemed "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides daily updates on air quality, indicating how clean or polluted the air is and highlighting potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically deteriorating during winter and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths globally each year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

Messi nets brace to win in first match after Argentina exit
item.description:
Lionel Messi scored twice to help Inter Miami rout DC United 4-0 on Saturday, taking a victory in his first match since saying farewell to the Argentina national team.
Four nights after scoring in his final match for the Albiceleste in a victory over Benin, the 39-year-old South American superstar struck in the 47th and 60th minutes as defending MLS champion Miami won for only the second time in their past 11 league matches.
A first-half brace by Luis Suarez staked the Herons to the lead as they improved to 13-5 with 10 drawn for 49 points, jumping from third to second in the Eastern Conference
Messi hopes to make Miami the first team to win back-to-back MLS crowns since the Los Angeles Galaxy in 2011-12.
Messi, the top point producer in the league with 23 goals plus assists on 13 others, seeks a third consecutive MLS Most Valuable Player award.
Uruguayan striker Suarez scored in the third minute to give Miami the lead, blasting a left-footed shot from the heart of the box into the top left corner.
Suarez struck again in the 39th for his 16th goal of the campaign, assisted like his first of the night by German Berterame.
Messi blasted home a left-footed shot off an assist from Suarez to give Miami a 3-0 lead and evaded three defenders to add another goal 13 minutes later as the pink-clad hosts pulled away to stay.
In other games, Scottish striker Lewis Morgan and American Djordje Mihailovic scored in second-half stoppage time to rally Toronto for a 2-1 home victory over Montreal.
The visitors grabbed the lead in the Canadian clash on a goal by Mexican forward Daniel Rios in the 52nd minute.
Toronto, however, battled back for the equalizer by winger Morgan, obtained last month from San Diego, in the third minute of stoppage time, his first regular-season MLS goal in two years.
Former Montreal standout Mihailovic struck for the decider in the fifth minute of extra time.
"Now I've scored on both sides of this derby," he said. "It feels good."
Toronto snapped a three-game losing streak to pull within a point of an East playoff berth.
At Chicago, Swiss forward Maren Haile-Selassie scored in the 87th minute to give the 10-man Chicago Fire a 2-1 triumph over New York City.
Austrian midfielder Hannes Wolf gave City the lead in the 19th minute and Chicago dropped to 10 men when Ivory coast midfielder Dje D'Avilla received his second yellow card in the 43rd minute.
Swede Anton Saletros equalized for Chicago in the 55th minute, setting the stage for the decider.

item.title: Barca extend perfect streak, Real survive Vinicius red
item.description:
Anthony Gordon scored his first goal for Barcelona as the Spanish champions extended their perfect start in La Liga with a 3-0 win over Getafe on Saturday.
Real Madrid finished with 10 men against Villarreal after Vinicius Junior was sent off for hair pulling in a 1-0 victory, with Yan Diomande's goal keeping Jose Mourinho's side, third, on Barcelona's trail.
Los Blancos are six points behind Barca, who also lead second-place Atletico Madrid by five points after Diego Simeone's team snatched a late 2-1 win at Alaves.
England winger Gordon opened the scoring for Barca in the second minute and Gabriel Jesus added another after half an hour for the league leaders, who have won every match they have played this season.
France defender Jules Kounde tucked home the third from Lamine Yamal's cross to cap Barca's solid win against Jose Bordalas's side at Camp Nou.
Barca were without their top scorer Raphinha, who sustained a hamstring problem during the international break with Brazil.
Flick replaced him with former Arsenal striker and Selecao compatriot Jesus and his side came roaring out of the blocks.
"Being at Barca is a dream... playing with these players is very easy too, everyone plays very well," Jesus told DAZN after his first start and third goal for the club.
"That makes it easier for me as a striker, to have chances, and I'm ready to score the goals...
"(But) I hope Rafa can recover quickly, because of course the team misses him."
Gordon, who has impressed since joining this summer, grabbed his first Barca goal with a low deflected effort after bundling his way past three players.
He was Barca's brightest spark in the first half, continuing his fine goalscoring form for England in the recent Nations League matches.
"He's doing very well," said Flick of Gordon. "He scored with England. He has a lot of confidence... he gives us a lot."
Getafe defender Zaid Romero gave the ball away in his own box for Barca's second, passing it straight to Jesus, who stroked into the bottom corner.
The otherwise quiet Yamal supplied Kounde for the third as Barca secured a ninth win from nine games across all competitions.
Diomande, Real Madrid's record 140-million-euro ($157 million) signing, scored his first goal for the club to help them shade Villarreal, but the game was marked by Vinicius's dismissal.
The Brazil international, on as a substitute, scored but his goal was disallowed and he was sent off after a VAR review showed he pulled the hair of Villarreal's Nathan Saliba in the build-up.
"Sorry to my team and the fans," said Vinicius on Instagram.
Mourinho's Madrid battled through the final stages with 10 men but held on to their slender lead earned by 19-year-old winger Diomande.
Despite Madrid's victory, Vinicius's red card left a bitter taste for Los Blancos, with the winger running the risk of a potential ban which could keep him out of the Clasico on October 25.
"I don't know what's going on with the referees, with this red card, I don't understand, but the most important thing is the victory," said Madrid midfielder Aurelien Tchouameni.
Mourinho declined to attend his post-match press conference in protest at the refereeing, a club source said.
The Madrid coach had complained bitterly about refereeing decisions which did not go his team's way in the derby defeat by Atletico before the recent international break.
Striker Kylian Mbappe was fit to start the match for Madrid and hit the post in a largely dull first half.
Home fans were not happy with the team at half-time but after 63 minutes they were able to celebrate Diomande's first goal, a sharp low finish into the far corner after being set up by Federico Valverde.
The drama with Vinicius followed, but in part thanks to goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois, Madrid were able to clinch three important points.
Earlier Cristian Romero's header in the 87th minute earned Atletico Madrid a narrow win at 10-man Alaves.
Alejandro Grimaldo put Atletico in front before Lucas Boye equalised from the penalty spot for Alaves before the interval.
Angel Perez was sent off for the hosts in the second half and Romero's header from Alex Baena's cross late on secured the victory.
"It's always important that the goal comes from wherever it comes, as long as it comes," said Simeone.

item.title: Ten-man Spurs rescue draw at Man Utd, Arsenal survive Leeds scare
item.description:
Ten-man Tottenham salvaged a 1-1 against fellow strugglers Manchester United thanks to Dominic Solanke's last-gasp leveller, while Arsenal got back on track as the champions survived a scare to beat Leeds 2-1 on Saturday.
In a clash dubbed 'El Sackicko' given the scrutiny on both managers, Bryan Mbeumo put United ahead in the 73rd minute at Old Trafford.
Mbeumo punished sloppy Tottenham marking to fire home from an acute angle after Matheus Cunha's pass picked him out in the penalty area.
Tottenham looked doomed when Uruguay midfielder Rodrigo Bentancur was sent off for headbutting United defender Luke Shaw in a brawl five minutes after United's opener.
But Solanke came to Tottenham's rescue in the final moments when he evaded United defender Lisandro Martinez to head in Sandro Tonali's cross.
It was a dramatic finale to a scrappy encounter in keeping with the problems gripping two underachieving teams.
Tottenham sit third bottom of the table and remain winless after losing three of their first six league games.
United are languishing in 12th place with only one league so far this season.
Roberto De Zerbi saved Tottenham from relegation on the final day of last term after taking charge late in the campaign.
But despite spending over £300 million ($429 million) on new signings in the close-season, Tottenham have failed to win any of their opening six games of a league season for just the fourth time in their history.
"I like the situation we were in with the red card. We need this situation. We have not accepted the defeat," De Zerbi said.
"I kiss Bentancur in the dressing room. Football is character. I'm very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character."
Carrick's side were hoping to build on last season's impressive third-place finish.
However, United's total of six points is their fewest at this stage of a campaign since 1986-87.
"For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time," Carrick said after United were booed off.
"It hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment."
After a shock 3-0 defeat at Brighton before the international break, Arsenal were in danger of a second successive loss when they fell behind at the Emirates Stadium.
James Justin fired Leeds ahead in the 55th minute after Arsenal failed to clear Gabriel Gudmundsson's cross.
But Italy defender Riccardo Calafiori found the cure when he converted Ben White's header from close-range in the 62nd minute.
Arsenal showcased their strength in depth as substitute Bruno Guimaraes drilled the winner from the edge of the area just six minutes after coming on.
Guimaraes' first goal at the Emirates since his close-season move from Newcastle made it five wins from six league matches for the Gunners.
The north London club sit in second place behind crisis-hit Manchester City on goal difference.
City travel to Liverpool on Sunday for their first match since being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules.
"We weren't pleased against Brighton and today was an opportunity to put that right. We certainly reacted in the manner we expected," Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said.
At Stamford Bridge, Chelsea's blistering start paved the way for a 5-1 rout of Bournemouth as the Blues won for the first time in four league matches.
Jordan Henderson gave Xabi Alonso's team the perfect start when the veteran midfielder curled home after just 68 seconds to claim his first goal for Chelsea.
The Blues struck again in the third minute through Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro made it three soon after half-time.
Evanilson got one back for Bournemouth in the 51st minute as Chelsea's run without a league clean-sheet extended to 22 matches.
Joao Pedro put the result beyond doubt in the 67th minute and Henderson, 36, bagged his second in the 70th minute with a fierce free-kick.
Aston Villa's troubled start continued with a disappointing 2-2 home draw against Brentford.
Ipswich beat winless Fulham 2-1, while 10-man Brighton won 2-0 at Sunderland to cement their hold on third place.

item.title: Rahmat Shah leads Afghan fightback against Bangladesh
item.description:
Skipper Rahmat Shah showed a grit and impeccable determination to keep Bangladesh bowlers at bay as Afghanistan fought back to leave the one-off Test evenly poised on Day 2 at the Sheikh Jayed Stadium in Abu Dhabi, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) on Saturday.
Rahmat negotiated Bangladesh bowlers astutely throughout the day to remain not out on 84, steering Afghanistan to 211-4 at stumps. Ikram Ali Khil was on 26 after adding 72 runs with the skipper for an unbroken fifth wicket.
Afghanistan are still trailing by runs 135 runs.
Bangladesh were bowled out for 346 in its first innings, riding on half-centuries from openers Tanzid Hasan Tamim (83), Shadman Islam (67) and wicket-keeper batter Liton Das (53).
The platform of Afghan resurgence was set by opener Abdul Malik, who hit his maiden half-century before being out on 62.
Afghanistan began watchfully and kept Bangladesh waiting for 11 overs for the first wicket.
Hasan Mahmud, the hero of Darwin Test victory over Australia, gave the side the breakthrough, getting rid of Sediqullah Atal for 17.
The stubbornness of Malik made Bangladesh toiling before Ebadot struck with the wicket of Shahidullah who made 20.
However, Rahmat joined Malik to keep Bangladesh bowlers at bay, denying them making further inroads.
Bangladesh heaved a sigh of relief in the last session when they got two wickets in quick succession.
Ebadot struck again with a delivery that carried extra bounce and Malik edged behind, ending a 70-run partnership with Rahmat.
Two overs later, Mehidy Hasan Miraz had Hasmathullah Shahidi stumped for duck, leaving Afghanistan 139-4.
Bangladesh appeared to take the stranglehold from that stage. But Rahmat, with apt support from Ikram Alikhil defied Bangladesh attack to leave the side unscathed till the stumps.
Ebadot was the most successful bowler for Bangladesh with 2-50 while Hasan and Miraz picked up one wicket apiece.
Earlier, Bangladesh added 29 runs to their overnight total of 317-8, with overnight unbeaten batter Nayeem Hasan scoring most of the runs to remain unbeaten on 35.
Afghan pacer Mohammad Saleem claimed the wicket of Taijul Isalm for 9 to finish with team-best 4-82.
Yamin Ahmadzai dismissed Ebadot Hossain for duck, snapping up 3-79.

item.title: PM mourns death of senior journalist Amir Khasru
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Saturday expressed deep sorrow over the death of veteran journalist and former Voice of America correspondent Amir Khasru.
In a condolence message, the prime minister hailed Khasru’s role as a journalist in support of democracy, truth and reason.
“His writings have always been a strong voice in support of democracy, truth, and reason,” he said.
Tarique Rahman prayed for the salvation of Khasru’s departed soul and conveyed his profound sympathy to the bereaved family.
Amir Khasru breathed his last while undergoing treatment in the intensive care unit (ICU) of Bangladesh Medical University in Dhaka earlier in the day.
He had long been suffering from various complications involving his kidneys and liver.
Khasru worked for Voice of America for many years and had experience working with several other media organizations.

item.title: UN report identifies key barriers to adolescent sexual health care in Asia-Pacific
item.description:
Financial hardship, legal restrictions and gaps in health services are preventing adolescents across Asia and the Pacific from accessing essential sexual and reproductive health care, according to a United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) report.
Titled 650 Million Reasons: Achieving Universal Health Coverage for Adolescent Sexual and Reproductive Health in Asia and the Pacific, the report examines policies, laws and health data across 30 low- and middle-income countries. Developed with the Burnet Institute, it finds that services remain fragmented and underfunded despite widespread policy commitments, leaving many adolescents without essential information, protection and care.
Asia and the Pacific is home to nearly 650 million adolescents aged 10–19, almost half the world's total. The report says meeting their health needs is essential to achieving universal health coverage, which ensures everyone can access quality health services without financial hardship.
According to the findings, up to 65% of adolescent girls in countries with available data report financial difficulties accessing health care. An average gap of 3 years separates the legal age of consent to sex from the legal age of consent to health care, while only 9 of the 30 countries provide clear guidance on accessing contraception without parental consent.
In most countries covered by the report, fewer than half of sexually active adolescent girls who need family planning services are able to use contraception.
The report also identifies judgmental treatment, discrimination and concerns about privacy as barriers to care. Even when services are free, transportation costs, informal fees and uncertainty about entitlements can prevent adolescents from seeking help.
“For an adolescent who cannot afford care or is turned away because of their age or marital status, a policy commitment offers little protection,” said Pio Smith, UNFPA Regional Director for Asia and the Pacific.
“Governments must turn those commitments into services young people can access, afford and trust. Investing in their health protects their choices, their education and their futures,” he added.
The report finds that most countries recognize adolescents in national health policies and have standards for services tailored to their needs. However, contradictory laws, insufficient financing and uneven implementation undermine these commitments.
It outlines 7 priorities for reform, including making adolescent sexual and reproductive health central to national health coverage plans, securing sustainable financing and improving the quality and reach of services.
Other priorities include reviewing discriminatory restrictions, clarifying consent rules, strengthening health information and community support, and involving adolescents in decisions about their care.
UNFPA has urged governments, development partners and civil society to translate the recommendations into funded action, with particular attention to adolescents who are out of school, displaced, living in poverty or otherwise excluded from services.
The report says universal health coverage will remain an unfinished promise until adolescents can access the care they need.

Russian strikes kill 11 including 3 children
item.description:
Russian strikes on Ukraine’s southeastern city of Zaporizhzhia on Saturday killed at least 11 people, including three children, according to regional authorities.
Ukrainian national police said Russia had targeted residential neighborhoods in the city with “five guided aerial bombs” early Saturday morning, hitting two residential buildings.
The strikes came a day after Ukrainian and European officials met in Miami in a renewed diplomatic push to end Russia’s war in Ukraine.
“The toll from the air strikes on Zaporizhzhia continues to rise. At present, 11 civilians have been killed. Among them are three children,” said Mykhailo Semikin, head of Zaporizhzhia Regional Military Administration.
He said rescuers were continuing their search for people under the rubble.
An AFP correspondent at the scene saw people being pulled from the rubble by Ukrainian emergency services.
“We saw people under the rubble -- a woman, her husband and a child,” one volunteer rescuer, Daniil Pishkin, told AFP.
He added that he saw two people rescued from the wreckage but “unfortunately there was a little girl who died.”
A resident of one of the buildings that was hit, who identified herself as Iryna, 69, said she just had time to seek refuge in the toilets after receiving an air raid warning.
She said her two neighbors were killed.
“They were 75 years old. They were simply thrown out there, onto the street. They didn’t make it to the hospital,” she told AFP.
The Zaporizhzhia region, located just a few dozen kilometers from the front line, and its capital by the same name have been the target of frequent strikes.
Russia has intensified its strikes on Ukrainian territory in recent months, causing a growing number of civilian casualties.
Diplomatic efforts mediated by the United States to end the war more than four years since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine have so far yielded no results.

item.title: Yemen govt forces say advancing against Houthis around key waterway
item.description:
Yemeni military sources told AFP on Saturday their forces were advancing against the Houthis in areas around the Bab al-Mandab strait but have not yet secured control of the waterway, after the government launched an operation to capture lost territory.
The Saudi-backed government last week announced a counter-offensive aimed at retaking all areas held by the Houthis, after the pro-Iran group seized Yemen’s entire western coastline in a lightning offensive.
The Houthis confirmed that government forces had attacked in the Bab al-Mandab area but they claimed to have repelled the assault.
“Saudi-led forces attempted to advance from the Ras al-Ara area in Lahj governorate towards the area south of Bab al-Mandab,” Hizam al-Asad, a member of the Houthis’ political bureau, told AFP.
“However, our forces repelled them outside the Bab al-Mandab zone, inflicting heavy losses in personnel and equipment and forcing the survivors to retreat.
“Our forces maintain control over Bab al-Mandab, Mayun Island, and the remaining areas along the country’s western coast,” he said.
Sources from the military of Yemen’s internationally recognized government also said Mayun Island -- located in the heart of the strait -- remained in Houthi hands as fighting continued.
Claims by the warring parties have been impossible to independently verify, with the situation moving fast on the ground and access for journalists difficult.
Clashes in western Yemen, specifically around the strait, had killed at least 63 people in the past 24 hours, military sources from both sides told AFP on Saturday.
Thirty-five members of government forces had been killed, while 28 Houthis had died, the sources said.
On Friday a Yemeni military source confirmed to AFP that their forces had launched a “major operation” in the strait region, supported by air power from Saudi Arabia, which backs Yemen’s government.
After four years of relative calm, Yemen’s civil war reignited in July before the Houthi gains on Yemen’s western coastline.
Saudi Arabia leads an international military coalition helping the Yemeni government fight the Houthis.
Early on Saturday the coalition said it had destroyed more than 130 Houthi targets in a “large-scale operation.”
The Houthis’ Al-Masirah TV channel reported on Saturday that enemy strikes had targeted the Bab al-Mandab area.
It also reported four Saudi strikes on the capital Sanaa’s international airport on Saturday, a day after saying two were killed in a Saudi strike on the airport.
In addition to battling Yemeni government forces on the ground, the Houthis have also been firing on targets inside Saudi Arabia, attacking transport hubs, oil facilities and other civilian sites with drones and missiles.
Riyadh said Friday that attacks on the Saudi capital’s international airport had killed three people the previous day.
Saudi Arabia has been retaliating with strikes on key Houthi targets inside Yemen. Houthi media reported on Friday that two people had died in attacks on the airport in the Houthi-controlled capital Sanaa.
Ordinary civilians have been paying the price for the renewed fighting in one of the world’s poorest countries, with more than 200,000 people displaced since July, according to UN data.

item.title: Turkiye social media ban for under-15s takes effect Nov 1
item.description:
Turkiye on Saturday formally declared a ban on the use of social media for under-15s, scheduled to come into effect on November 1.
It has joined a growing number of countries legislating to protect children and teenagers from the harmful effects of online platforms.
The official state journal published the decision following the adoption of a law by parliament in April.
It stipulates that social media providers must “take the necessary technical and administrative measures, including age verification, to implement” protections for young people.
“No service likely to produce an addictive effect in children may be offered.”
Countries including Australia have introduced restrictions on social media for children and others such as Britain and France are pushing to do the same.
They aim to protect children from digital risks such as screen addiction, lack of sleep, bullying and eating disorders.
Rights groups have complained of restrictions on freedom of expression in Turkiye targeting LGBTQ communities, the media and the political opposition. Numerous social media accounts have been blocked in recent weeks.

Dengue: Four more die, 1,935 hospitalized in 24 hours
item.description:
Four people died of dengue, and 1,631 were hospitalized with the Aedes mosquito-borne disease in the last 24 hours till 8am on Saturday, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
With this development, the country has recorded 299 deaths from dengue this year.
Of the new dengue cases, 703 were recorded in Dhaka division, 61 in Mymensingh division, 234 in Chittagong division, 184 in Khulna division, 141 in Rajshahi division, 75 in Rangpur division, 219 in Barisal division and 14 in Sylhet division.
A total of 97,082 dengue patients have so far been hospitalized across the country this year, according to the DGHS report.
However, in the last 24 hours, 1,627 patients recovered and were discharged from hospitals.
So far, 91,007 dengue patients have recovered and returned home after receiving treatment this year.
A total of 102,861 people were infected with dengue, and 413 people died from the disease last year.

item.title: Bangladesh discusses €250 million loan for women's health initiative
item.description:
Bangladesh discussed a proposed €250 million loan from the European Investment Bank (EIB) to implement a women's health initiative with international development partners during the World Health Summit (WHS) 2026 in Berlin, Germany, on Saturday.
The bilateral and technical discussions took place at the Charité campus in Berlin, involving a high-level delegation from the Bangladesh government and international development partners.
The Bangladesh delegation was led by Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain and Special Assistant to the Prime Minister on Health Ziauddin Hyder.
The proposed Women's Health Initiative aims to reduce maternal mortality, ensure early detection of cervical and breast cancers, and develop modern facilities to provide round-the-clock emergency obstetric services at the union level.
The discussions also covered strengthening district hospitals and introducing a digital patient-tracking system.
The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin, and the Berlin Institute of Health (BIH) are providing technical and strategic support for the initiative.
Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain said: “This international partnership will play an important role in ensuring quality healthcare for women and girls in remote areas of Bangladesh.”
The Bangladesh delegation also visited Charité Hospital in Berlin to observe its medical facilities and cancer screening services.
The parties agreed to form a joint working group to support the future development of healthcare systems in both countries.

item.title: Abdul Awal Mintoo: Bangladesh, India to hold talks on elephant corridor in Sherpur
item.description:
Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Abdul Awal Mintoo on Saturday said the government would soon initiate talks with India under an existing protocol to establish a cross-border corridor for wild elephants roaming the Garo Hills in Sherpur.
Around 130 to 135 wild elephants that came from India's Meghalaya have become stranded in the Garo Hills of Sherpur as border fencing has prevented them from returning to their habitat, he said.
The minister said the government would request the Indian authorities to open gates in the fencing to allow the elephants to return, although previous requests had not received a positive response.
At the same time, initiatives would be taken to develop forest areas in Sherpur into safe habitats for the elephants, he added.
The minister made the remarks while speaking at a discussion on resolving human-elephant conflict and conserving wild elephants at Madhutila Eco Park in Nalitabari upazila of Sherpur.
He said the scenic Garo Hills, its wild elephants and the surrounding natural environment would be used to develop the area into a tourism hub. This would create economic opportunities for local people while helping protect elephants and reduce human-elephant conflict, he added.
The Sherpur district administration and the Mymensingh Forest Division organized the discussion with lawmakers from elephant-affected areas, Elephant Response Team (ERT) members, journalists and volunteers involved in elephant conservation. Deputy Commissioner Farida Yesmin chaired the event.
Sherpur-2 lawmaker Engineer Fahim Chowdhury, Chief Conservator of Forests Md Amir Hossain Chowdhury, Conservator of Forests for the Wildlife and Nature Conservation Region Md Sanaullah Patwari, Central Region Conservator of Forests ASM Zahir Uddin Akon, Mymensingh Divisional Forest Officer Kazi Muhammad Nurul Karim and Police Superintendent AKM Johirul Islam spoke as special guests.

item.title: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee detained by Delhi Police; CJP demands release
item.description:
YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was detained by Delhi Police at his residence in Gurugram’s Sector 56 on Saturday ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) planned protest at Jantar Mantar, NDTV reported, citing police sources.
Rathee had arrived to join the demonstration, prompting heightened security arrangements across the national capital.
According to sources, around 50 Delhi Police personnel arrived at Rathee’s Gurugram residence on Saturday morning and detained him.
The detention drew a sharp response from the CJP, which demanded his “immediate release”.
On Friday evening, Rathee announced his participation in Saturday’s protest in a video posted on his X account.
A vocal critic of the Narendra Modi government, Rathee arrived in India from Germany earlier this week and joined a CJP protest in Bengaluru on October 8.
Rathee has a substantial online following, with 19.2 million Instagram followers, 3.3 million on X, and 33 million YouTube subscribers.
Earlier this week, Delhi Police denied permission for the protest, citing security concerns and procedural requirements.
Police have stepped up preventive detentions and deployed personnel at strategic locations to prevent protesters from reaching the protest site.
More than 400 people were detained overnight, while hundreds of trains were cancelled and dozens of metro stations shut ahead of a large-scale protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in central Delhi on Saturday.
The CJP mobilised supporters to gather at Jantar Mantar, while the Centre deployed more than 20,000 police and Central Armed Police Forces personnel to maintain law and order.

item.title: Tagore mural targeted outside Shilpakala Academy, one detained
item.description:
Police detained ANM Ayas, a leader of Rashtra Sanglap Forum, on Saturday afternoon for allegedly attempting to deface a mural of Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore outside Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy in the capital’s Segunbagicha area.
The incident occurred just five days after Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) cleared the footpath of encroachments and decorated an adjoining wall with portraits of 10 prominent figures from Bengali literature, art and culture.
Shahbag Police Station Sub-Inspector Abdul Khalek confirmed the detention, saying Ayas had been taken to the police station after attempting to erase Tagore’s portrait.
The incident comes amid criticism over the selection of cultural personalities featured in the murals, particularly the inclusion of figures from West Bengal and the absence of women.
According to reports, police intervened after an attempt was made to apply black or white paint to the portraits outside the academy.
The Daily Campus reported that three people, including Ayas, were detained in connection with the incident. Other reports initially confirmed only Ayas’s detention.
The Daily Campus also described Ayas as president of Rashtra Sanglap Forum, while other outlets identified him as its member secretary.
On October 5, DSCC reopened the Segunbagicha footpath following an operation to remove encroachments.
As part of the renovation, portraits of 10 cultural figures were painted on a roadside wall near Shilpakala Academy.
They included Rabindranath Tagore, national poet Kazi Nazrul Islam, Shilpacharya Zainul Abedin, filmmaker Satyajit Ray, philosopher and social reformer Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, Fakir Lalon Shah, artist SM Sultan, filmmaker Zahir Raihan, folk singer Shah Abdul Karim and actor Humayun Faridi.
The project also included new dustbins, benches for pedestrians and repairs to the boundary wall.
The newly renovated stretch was opened to pedestrians after the removal of makeshift shops and other obstructions.
It was not immediately clear whether any formal case had been filed or what further legal action police intended to take.

item.title: PM assures support for waste-to-fuel technology
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Saturday assured support for a technology that could turn waste into fuel oil and help reduce Bangladesh’s dependence on imported energy.
He gave the assurance as a team of researchers led by Khulna University of Engineering and Technology (Kuet) Professor Dr Md Khalequzzaman briefed him on the technology at his office in Tejgaon, said a release issued by the PM’s Press Wing.
The technology uses a process known as hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) to convert human waste, waste from sewage treatment plants, kitchen waste and agricultural residues into fuel oil.
The researchers said they have been working on the technology for around 10 years and have achieved a 50–55% biocrude yield in laboratory tests. They have also made progress in producing biocrude with a high diesel content.
The next step is to set up a pilot plant capable of processing one to three tons of waste daily to assess the technology’s efficiency, production costs and commercial viability. The estimated cost of the pilot project is Tk100–120 crore.
According to the researchers, the technology, if developed for commercial-scale production, could replace around 10–15% of imported crude oil and save foreign currency equivalent to Tk6,500–13,000 crore annually.
However, the estimates would need to be validated through large-scale technical and economic assessments, they said.
The researchers said the technology could also help reduce environmental pollution, improve waste management and create opportunities for developing a domestic fuel industry.
The Prime Minister assured them of the government’s necessary cooperation in advancing the initiative.
Power and Energy Minister Iqbal Mahmood Tuku, State Minister Anindya Islam Amit, University Grants Commission member Professor Abdullah Al Mamun, Kuet Vice-Chancellor Professor Mohammad Masud and Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation Chairman Dr Mohammad Rafiqul Islam were present at the briefing.

item.title: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, two others detained aboard plane in Delhi
item.description:
Police detained Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijit Dipke and two other party members aboard an aircraft shortly after it landed at Delhi Airport, ahead of the party’s planned protest at Jantar Mantar, reports NDTV.
Dipke went live on Instagram as police entered the aircraft. The video shows officers detaining Dipke, Sourav Das and Ashutosh Ranka inside the plane.
The footage captures a commotion as CJP members questioned the police over their decision to detain them before passengers had disembarked.
In the video, Dipke is heard telling female police officers: “You could have waited for us to step out. Come, arrest us. We are not afraid.”

item.title: States told by Indian govt to stop protest march to Delhi
item.description:
India’s Union Ministry of Home Affairs has asked all states and Union Territories to coordinate with Delhi Police and take preventive measures to stop protesters from travelling to the national capital ahead of a planned demonstration by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), The Hindu reported.
In a letter to state chief secretaries and police chiefs on Friday, Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan flagged the “grave law and order and public order implications” of the planned protest at Jantar Mantar on Saturday.
The protesters are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over concerns about the Election Commission’s functioning and its handling of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Authorities have introduced sweeping restrictions ahead of the demonstration. These include preventive detentions, train cancellations, the closure of metro stations and the suspension of mobile internet services in parts of central Delhi.
The restrictions have drawn criticism from protest organisers, who have described the measures as intimidation by the authorities.
In its letter, the Union government said Delhi Police had rejected the organisers’ request to hold the demonstration at Jantar Mantar, ANI reported.
The ministry also cited what it described as a “documented history of non-compliance with lawful directions” by the CJP and organisations supporting it during an earlier protest. It alleged that the previous demonstration, involving participants from several states, had disrupted public order and damaged public property, The Hindu reported.
The ministry said intelligence inputs suggested that CJP members and supporters planned to defy prohibitory orders and enter Delhi through multiple routes.
It directed states and Union Territories to “immediately operationalise preventive measures” in coordination with Delhi Police to maintain public order and protect critical infrastructure.
The government also stressed the need for real-time intelligence sharing among state agencies, transit authorities and Delhi Police to ensure coordinated action.
The planned demonstration follows several days of protests by opposition INDIA bloc members in Delhi and other parts of India, calling for Kumar’s resignation over concerns about electoral roll revisions and the functioning of the Election Commission.

item.title: Mahatma Gandhi’s great-grandson detained in Mumbai ahead of CJP protest
item.description:
Mumbai Police detained Tushar Gandhi, great-grandson of Mahatma Gandhi and president of Hum Bharat Ke Log, along with his associates on Saturday as they headed to August Kranti Maidan for a protest in support of the Cockroach Janata Party’s (CJP) demonstration in Delhi, The Indian Express reported.
The protest was scheduled for 3:30pm.
A police official said Gandhi was picked up from Bandra and taken to DN Nagar police station. Gandhi claimed on X that he had been arrested and taken to an unknown location. Police denied arresting him, saying he had only been detained.
Guddi S L, vice-president of the organisation, was picked up from Andheri and taken to MIDC police station, police confirmed.
On Friday, Gandhi posted a poster on X urging Mumbaikars to join him at August Kranti Maidan, the site from which the Quit India movement was launched in 1942. The protest was planned in support of the CJP’s demand for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
Gamdevi Police said no application had been received or permission granted for the demonstration.
“Due to a Supreme Court ruling, the Mumbai police cannot grant permission to hold a protest at August Kranti Maidan as the land belongs to the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). No one had approached us in the first instance,” a senior police official said on Friday.
Guddi disputed the claim, saying she had emailed police seeking permission because Gandhi was not in the city but had received no response.
“Gandhi has been called by the police, and they are telling him not to protest. They have also asked him about his location and said that they would detain him,” she said on Friday.
The detentions come amid heightened police vigilance across Maharashtra ahead of the CJP’s planned protest at Jantar Mantar. Police in Mumbai and other parts of the state have been monitoring people suspected of planning to travel to Delhi.
Mumbai Police detained more than 200 people on Friday to prevent them from travelling to the national capital, the report said.

item.title: Two crude bombs hurled outside PM’s Office, police seek suspects
item.description:
Two crude bombs, were hurled outside the Prime Minister’s Office in Tejgaon, Dhaka, early Saturday, prompting police to launch an investigation to identify and arrest those involved.
The incident occurred around 1:15am. One of the bombs exploded, while the other was safely detonated in a controlled explosion by the Bomb Disposal Unit of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s (DMP) Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit.
DMP Tejgaon Division Deputy Commissioner Ibne Mizan said police were working to identify and arrest the two suspects who arrived on a motorcycle.
According to him, the two men reached the area around 1:15am, surveyed their surroundings for two to three minutes, hurled the bombs and fled. Police received information that they headed towards Kafrul via Agargaon.
Ibne Mizan said police teams began investigating immediately after the incident. Footage from nearby CCTV cameras has been collected to help identify the suspects, and the incident is being treated as a priority.

item.title: Job seekers block roads in Dhaka over youth development exam paper leak
item.description:
Job seekers blocked several major roads in Dhaka on Saturday to protest the alleged leak of question papers for the Department of Youth Development’s recruitment examination, disrupting traffic in several areas.
Around noon, protesters blocked the road in front of Mirpur Bangla College near the Technical intersection.
Job seekers also took to the streets in Motijheel and at the Aarong intersection in Asad Gate, bringing traffic to a standstill in the affected areas.
The protesters questioned why question paper leaks were still occurring under the current government, recalling that such incidents had also taken place under the previous regime. They questioned the significance of the July 2024 uprising, in which thousands of people sacrificed their lives.
They demanded that the government identify those responsible and ensure exemplary punishment, as well as take strict measures to prevent similar incidents in the future.
Afzal Hossain, a job seeker, said he had travelled hundreds of kilometres from a remote area to Dhaka to sit for the examination.
“After enduring so much hardship to reach the exam centre, I learned that the examination had been postponed because the question paper had been leaked,” he said.
“Who will compensate the thousands of us who went to such lengths to sit for the examination? We demand exemplary punishment for everyone involved in the question paper leak,” he added.

item.title: Humaiun: Bangladesh views Makkah Defence Agreement positively
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Saturday said Bangladesh was positively considering the Makkah Defence Agreement, with any decision to be guided by national interests and the potential contribution of the country's peacekeeping expertise to regional peace and stability.
“We are having positive discussions on the Makkah Defence Agreement. We are viewing it positively,” he said while addressing a national seminar at the Foreign Service Academy in the capital.
Kobir said Bangladesh could take a favourable decision if the agreement served its national interests and its peacekeeping expertise could contribute to the welfare of Muslim nations and help maintain peace and stability in the Middle East.
“If it falls within the national interests of Bangladesh and converges, and we feel that our peacekeeping expertise can add value in serving Muslim nations and keeping a stable, peaceful Middle East, then there is every scope to take a positive decision on the matter,” he said.
The Bangladesh Institute of International and Strategic Studies (BIISS) and the Center for Migration Studies of North South University (NSU) jointly organised the seminar titled “From Workforce to Strategic Partnership: Reimagining Bangladesh-KSA Relations.”
The state minister also said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman had accepted an invitation from Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince to visit the Kingdom.
“He has accepted and will do so at some point very soon,” Kobir said.
He said the Crown Prince had also expressed interest in visiting Bangladesh, adding that Dhaka would welcome him at a mutually convenient time.
Kobir said the proposed visits reflected growing political ties between the two countries. He also described Bangladesh as a strong partner of Saudi Arabia in maritime security.
Calling for a comprehensive economic and strategic partnership, he said bilateral relations should expand beyond their traditional focus on labour migration and remittances.
“While that foundation remains important, it cannot be the ceiling of our ambition,” he said.
He said Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 and Bangladesh's economic transformation had created common interests in investment, human capital, technology and connectivity.
Discussions were underway on a possible investment fund to facilitate joint investments and partnerships in priority sectors, he added.
The state minister identified renewable energy, infrastructure, ports, logistics, agriculture, fisheries, food security, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, information technology and artificial intelligence as promising areas for Saudi investment.
He said such investments required a predictable and transparent business environment, improved institutional coordination and timely decision-making.
Kobir stressed the need to shift towards trained and certified professionals to meet the changing demands of Saudi Arabia's labour market.
He called for stronger cooperation among training institutions, universities and industries to ensure skills certification aligned with Saudi market requirements.
The welfare, dignity and rights of Bangladeshi workers in Saudi Arabia would remain a government priority, he said.
Kobir also highlighted opportunities for knowledge and technology partnerships, alongside cooperation in ports, shipping, logistics, aviation and supply chains.
“The next chapter of Bangladesh-Saudi Arabia relations should therefore be defined by value creation rather than volume alone,” he said.
Saudi Arabia’s Ambassador to Bangladesh Dr Abdullah Zafer bin Abiyah addressed the seminar as the guest of honour. Foreign Ministry Secretary (Bilateral) Dr Md Nazrul Islam and Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Secretary Md Mokhtar Ahmed spoke as special guests.
BIISS Director General Major General A S M Ridwanur Rahman and NSU Vice-Chancellor Professor Abdul Hannan Chowdhury also addressed the seminar.
Speaking to journalists after the event, Kobir reiterated that peace and stability in the Middle East and the Muslim world were central to Bangladesh's consideration of the Makkah Defence Agreement.
He said maintaining peace in the region encompassing Makkah and Madinah was a key objective, adding that Bangladesh could deploy its peacekeeping expertise more effectively and extensively across the world.
He said initiatives regarding participation in the agreement or association with the alliance were being considered positively, with regional peace and stability remaining the priority.
Kobir said regular high-level exchanges, including ministerial and official visits in both directions, were strengthening bilateral engagement.
He also stressed the need to diversify employment opportunities into energy, technology and other promising sectors while sending more highly skilled professionals to Saudi Arabia.
“We are also holding very positive discussions with Saudi Arabia and, God willing, many new opportunities will emerge between the two countries,” he said.
The state minister said there was scope for a broad investment partnership under which Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia could jointly invest in profitable sectors.
“The days of dependency are over. We are now placing emphasis on an equal partnership between the two countries and on sustainable policies,” he told journalists.

item.title: Durga Puja festivities begin with observance of Mahalaya
item.description:
Mahalaya, which marks the beginning of Hindu community’s largest religious festival Durga Puja, is being observed across the country amid festivity on Saturday.
From early morning, temples across the country resonated with Chandipath, tarpan rituals, and devotional hymns in praise of Goddess Durga.
The serene autumn dawn ushered in Devipaksha, the fortnight dedicated to the goddess, through the traditional recitation of sacred verses.
Mahalaya that is considered as ceremonial invocation of goddess Durga is observed seven days prior to the initiation of the Durga Puja, the largest religious festival of the Hindu community.
Hindus believe the earth prepares itself and welcomes the coming of the Goddess and her children, through the celebration.
On this day, Hindus remember and pay homage to the deceased ancestors by performing a puja, and offering Brahmins clothes, food and sweets in their name.
From this day, the countdown to Durga Puja begins.
This year, Shashthi Puja will be celebrated on October 17 while Bijoya Dashami on October 21 will mark the goddess’s departure to Kailash.
Scriptures mention three major milestones of Durga Puja—Mahalaya, Bodhon, and Sandhi Puja. On Mahalaya, Goddess Durga receives the divine mandate to defeat the demon king Mahishasura.
Empowered by the combined forces of Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva, she emerges as `Mahashakti’, adorned with ten weapons and riding a lion, ultimately slaying Mahishasura after a nine-day battle.

Brazil’s Lula scraps gasoline tax ahead of runoff election
item.description:
Brazil’s government announced on Friday that gasoline taxes will be temporarily scrapped, two weeks ahead of the runoff election between incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flavio Bolsonaro.
Lula, who is seeking his fourth term, is trying to contain rising fuel prices amid a global spike in oil prices driven by the war in the Middle East.
The gasoline tax, which was set at 0.89 reais ($0.18) per liter, would be waived for 30 days, according to the government.
The measure announced on Friday also expands subsidies for importers of diesel, the predominant fuel used in Brazil’s freight transport.
“The objective is to ensure that imports remain viable at a critical moment for supply,” the presidency said in a statement.
The fiscal impact of the tax exemptions will be offset by Brazil’s “extraordinary revenues” from oil exports, it said.
The runoff election on October 25 was set after Lula won 45% of the vote in the first round and Bolsonaro received 47%.
Bolsonaro called his opponent “irresponsible,” warning that Lula was placing a “bomb” on consumers’ laps and that diesel prices could rise after the election.
Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former far-right president Jair Bolsonaro, repeatedly criticized the government during his campaign for failing to control the cost of living.
Inflation in Brazil rose by 0.82% in September, the statistics authority said on Friday.

Barrister Abdul Muntaquim Chaudhury dies at 97
item.description:
Barrister Abdul Muntaquim Chaudhury, a Bangladeshi politician, lawyer and organizer of the Liberation War, died in Melbourne, Australia, on October 9, 2026. He was 97.
Born on September 2, 1929, Chaudhury served as a member of Pakistan’s National Assembly in the 1960s and was re-elected in 1970. After Bangladesh gained independence, he became a member of the Constituent Assembly and helped draft the country’s constitution.
In 1973, he was appointed Bangladesh’s ambassador to Japan. He later served as the country’s ambassador to the German Democratic Republic.
After returning to Bangladesh in 1979, Chaudhury became the founding executive director of the Bangladesh Legal Aid and Services Trust (Blast).
Abu Taher Abdul Muntaquim Chaudhury, whose family descended from the Kanihati Chaudhury family of Sylhet, was the youngest child of Khan Bahadur Tazzammul Ali Chaudhury.
He completed his Intermediate of Arts (IA) at Aligarh Muslim University before studying at Santiniketan and St Xavier’s College. He earned his bachelor’s degree from the University of Calcutta and was later called to the bar at Lincoln’s Inn in London.

Dhaka’s air quality 4th worst in the world Saturday morning
item.description:
Dhaka, the overcrowded capital city of Bangladesh, has ranked 4th on the list of cities with the worst air quality, with an AQI index of 181 at 9:06am on Saturday.
Dhaka’s air was classified as "unhealthy", according to the air quality and pollution city ranking.
Singapore, Malaysia’s Kuala Lumpur and India's Kolkata occupied the first, second and third spots in the list, with AQI scores of 200, 198 and 192, respectively.
When the AQI value for particle pollution is between 101 and 150, air quality is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", between 150 and 200 is "unhealthy", between 201 and 300 is said to be "very unhealthy", while a reading of 301+ is considered "hazardous", posing serious health risks to residents.
The AQI, an index for reporting daily air quality, informs people how clean or polluted the air of a certain city is and what associated health effects might be a concern for them.
The AQI in Bangladesh is based on five pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), NO2, CO, SO2, and ozone.
Dhaka has long been grappling with air pollution issues. Its air quality usually turns unhealthy in winter and improves during the monsoon.
